name: Stratum Mid-Level Pressed Trouser
description: Charcoal poly-wool blend slacks with a permanent-press finish that survives a full transit commute without creasing. Side seams have hidden snap channels for standard leg prosthetics up to 40mm diameter. Sold in six inseam lengths, all identical cuts — conformity is the point.
functionality: Permanent-press finish, aug-compatible side seams, moisture-wicking inner lining.
what_it_says: You dress like everyone else on your floor, which is exactly what your supervisor wants.
story_hooks: A pair found in a lost-and-found bin has an access badge sewn into the waistband — still active.
The permanent-press chemical coating slowly releases a mild stress-suppressant absorbed through the skin; no one at Stratum is advertising this.

physical_description.visual_profile: Austere, utilitarian silhouette with a crisp, almost rigid drape. Straight-leg cut that reads as deliberately conformist — the uniform of Tier 3 transit workers and mid-level corporate drones. Sits at the ankle with minimal taper.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not form-fitting; designed for comfort during 8+ hour shifts. Waistband sits at natural hip level. Generous through the thigh and knee to accommodate prosthetic integration without visible bulging. Legs hang clean and parallel.
physical_description.primary_material: Charcoal poly-wool blend (60% polyester, 40% wool). Permanently press-treated with heat-set resin coating — fabric memory is engineered into the fiber structure.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost slick surface with subtle ribbed weave visible on close inspection. The permanent-press finish gives it a slightly waxy, low-friction feel. No natural softness; this is intentionally industrial.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal gray — neutral enough to pair with anything, dark enough to hide dirt from factory floors or transit grime. No patterns; absolute color uniformity across all pairs.
physical_description.closures: Standard front fly with magnetic snap (superior to zippers for rapid undressing in medical contexts). No buttons — all fastening is magnetic or friction-fit. Side seam integration uses recessed friction snaps flush with the weave.
distinctive_features: Hidden snap channels along both side seams (inset 8mm) for standard prosthetic leg attachments up to 40mm diameter
Reinforced internal gusset at crotch (ballistic weave insert) for durability during repetitive motion
Six standardized inseam lengths (28, 30, 32, 34, 36, 38 inches) — no custom tailoring offered
Stratum branding (small woven label, inner waistband only — no visible logos)
Thermal-regulation weave: moisture-wicking inner lining to prevent sweat accumulation during commutes
RFID pocket sewn into right hip seam (for transit pass or credential chip)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 — working-class standard issue. Not cheap enough to be Tier 4 salvage, not refined enough for Tier 1-2 corpo wear. This is the uniform of the functional middle.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by transit workers, mid-level manufacturing plant staff, medical facility orderlies, and corporate middle-management. Signals reliability and conformity — the wearer has accepted their place in the system. Common in the ungoverned zones among those trying to signal 'legitimacy' to corpo patrols.
physical_description.condition_typical: Perpetually pristine due to permanent-press coating. After 200+ wears, fabric begins to pill slightly at inner thighs and around the magnetic snap anchors. Magnetic snaps can wear out (friction causes micro-corrosion). Typical lifespan: 18-24 months before replacement.
